source.text: לַמְנַצֵּ֬חַ׀לִבְנֵי־קֹ֬רַח מִזְמֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: For the director, of [the] sons of Korah, a psalm.

en.L: For the director: of the sons of Korah. A psalm.
en.B: For the music director. Of the sons of Korah. A psalm.
en.R: For the leader of the music. A song from the family of Korah.

fr.L: Au chef de chœur : des fils de Coré. Un psaume.
fr.B: Au chef de chœur. Des fils de Coré. Un psaume.
fr.R: Pour le chef des musiciens. Un chant de la famille de Coré.

decisions.choice: The title is verse 1
decisions.reason: The title is part of the Hebrew text and is counted as verse 1, so the verse numbers here are one higher than in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: the director: the one who leads the music
decisions.reason: As in 4:1, probably the leader of the temple music.

decisions.choice: the sons of Korah: a family of Levite singers
decisions.reason: The descendants of Korah, a Levite (Numbers 26:11), served as gatekeepers and singers at the temple (1 Chronicles 9:19; 2 Chronicles 20:19). Eleven psalms carry their name (42-49, 84-85, 87-88). "Of" may mean the psalm belongs to their collection or was written by one of them.

decisions.choice: a wisdom psalm
decisions.reason: Psalm 49 is a teaching poem, like Proverbs and Job: it takes up the riddle of why the wicked rich prosper, and answers it with death, which no money can buy off, and with God, who ransoms the upright (verse 16). Psalm 73 asks the same question.

decisions.choice: song
decisions.reason: As in 3:1.

source.text: שִׁמְעוּ־זֹ֭את כָּל־הָֽעַמִּ֑ים הַ֝אֲזִ֗ינוּ כָּל־יֹ֥שְׁבֵי חָֽלֶד׃

records.literal_gloss: Hear this, all the peoples; give ear, all inhabitants of [the] world,

en.L: Hear this, all [you] peoples; give ear, all [you] inhabitants of [the] world,
en.B: Listen to this, all you nations; pay attention, everyone who lives in the world,
en.R: Listen, all you people of every nation! Everyone in the world, pay attention!

fr.L: Écoutez ceci, tous [les] peuples ; prêtez l’oreille, tous [les] habitants du monde,
fr.B: Écoutez ceci, vous toutes les nations ; soyez attentifs, vous tous qui habitez le monde,
fr.R: Écoutez, vous, les gens de toutes les nations ! Vous tous qui vivez dans le monde, faites attention !

decisions.choice: Hear, give ear: the opening of a wise teacher
decisions.reason: The double call to listen is how teachers of wisdom begin (Proverbs 4:1; Job 34:2). This lesson is for all people, not Israel only, because death comes to everyone.

decisions.choice: the world: the world of passing time
decisions.reason: The word (cheled) means the world, and is related to a word for a lifetime (39:6): a world where nothing lasts.

source.text: גַּם־בְּנֵ֣י אָ֭דָם גַּם־בְּנֵי־אִ֑ישׁ יַ֝֗חַד עָשִׁ֥יר וְאֶבְיֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: both children of humankind and children of man, together rich and needy.

en.L: both {{gender:children of humankind|sons of mankind}} and {{gender:children of people|sons of man}}, together rich and needy.
en.B: the humble and the great, the rich and the poor together.
en.R: It does not matter if you are important or not, rich or poor.

fr.L: aussi bien les {{gender:enfants des humains|fils des hommes}} que les {{gender:enfants de l’humain|fils de l’homme}}, ensemble riche et pauvre.
fr.B: petits et grands, riches et pauvres ensemble.
fr.R: Peu importe que vous soyez importants ou non, riches ou pauvres.

decisions.choice: children of humankind and children of man: people of low and high rank
alternatives: all people, every one of them
decisions.reason: The two phrases use two words for a human being ('adam and 'ish). Set side by side they seem to mean common people and people of rank, as in 62:10; the second half of the verse says the same with "rich and needy".

decisions.choice: children of humankind, children of people (L), with "sons of" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The phrases mean human beings of every kind (m1). Balanced says what they mean and needs no alternative.

decisions.choice: "enfants des humains" and "enfants de l'humain" at Literal, with "fils des hommes" and "fils de l'homme" as the alternatives
decisions.reason: The two phrases mean human beings of every rank (meaning decision m1). French puts the setting on the nouns, as the English does; Balanced and Readable say what the phrases mean and need no setting.

source.text: פִּ֭י יְדַבֵּ֣ר חָכְמ֑וֹת וְהָג֖וּת לִבִּ֣י תְבוּנֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: My mouth will speak wisdom, and [the] meditation of my heart [is] understanding.

en.L: My mouth will speak wisdom, and the meditation of my heart [will be] understanding.
en.B: What I say will be wise; what my heart has pondered will give insight.
en.R: I will tell you wise things. I have thought hard about them, and I understand.

fr.L: Ma bouche dira la sagesse, et la méditation de mon cœur [sera] intelligence.
fr.B: Ce que je vais dire sera sage ; ce que mon cœur a médité donnera l’intelligence.
fr.R: Je vais vous dire des choses sages. J’y ai beaucoup réfléchi, et je comprends.

decisions.choice: wisdom, understanding: plurals of fullness
decisions.reason: Both words are plural in form, meaning deep or complete wisdom and understanding.

decisions.choice: meditation: quiet, careful thought
decisions.reason: The word (hagut) is from the verb used in 1:2 for murmuring God's instruction to oneself: thought turned over and over.

source.text: אַטֶּ֣ה לְמָשָׁ֣ל אָזְנִ֑י אֶפְתַּ֥ח בְּ֝כִנּ֗וֹר חִידָתִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: I will incline to a proverb my ear; I will open with a lyre my riddle.

en.L: I will incline my ear to a proverb; I will open my riddle with [the] lyre.
en.B: I will listen closely to a proverb; to the music of the lyre I will lay open my riddle.
en.R: I will listen carefully to a wise saying. Then I will play the harp and explain a hard question.

fr.L: Je tendrai l’oreille à un proverbe ; j’ouvrirai mon énigme sur la lyre.
fr.B: J’écouterai attentivement un proverbe ; au son de la lyre j’exposerai mon énigme.
fr.R: J’écouterai avec attention une parole de sagesse. Puis je jouerai de la harpe et j’expliquerai une question difficile.

decisions.choice: proverb: a wise saying
decisions.reason: The word (mashal) is a saying, a comparison or a parable; here probably the refrain of verses 13 and 21, which compares people to animals.

decisions.choice: riddle: a hard question
decisions.reason: The word (chidah) is a riddle or a puzzle (Judges 14:12). The puzzle is why the wicked rich do well, and whether the upright should fear them (verse 6).

decisions.choice: incline my ear: the teacher first listens
decisions.reason: The teacher listens for the wisdom he passes on, as a prophet hears before he speaks; to open a riddle is to set it out or explain it.

decisions.choice: lyre: a stringed instrument
decisions.reason: The kinnor was a small stringed instrument, played by hand, as David did (1 Samuel 16:23).

source.text: לָ֣מָּה אִ֭ירָא בִּ֣ימֵי רָ֑ע עֲוֺ֖ן עֲקֵבַ֣י יְסוּבֵּֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: Why should I fear in days of evil, [when the] iniquity of my heels surrounds me,

en.L: Why should I fear in days of evil, [when] the iniquity of my heels surrounds me,
en.B: Why should I be afraid in evil times, when the wrongdoing of those who dog my steps closes in on me,
en.R: Why should I be afraid when times are bad? Why should I be afraid when cheaters are all around me?

fr.L: Pourquoi craindrais-je aux jours de malheur, [quand] la faute de mes talons m’entoure,
fr.B: Pourquoi aurais-je peur aux jours mauvais, quand la malice de ceux qui me talonnent se resserre sur moi,
fr.R: Pourquoi aurais-je peur quand les temps sont durs ? Pourquoi aurais-je peur quand des tricheurs sont tout autour de moi ?

decisions.choice: my heels: those at my heels, people who cheat me
alternatives: the wrong I have done at every step
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "the iniquity of my heels". The word for heel ('aqev) is the root of the name Jacob, who grabbed his brother's heel and later cheated him (Genesis 27:36), so "my heels" may be those who follow at my heels to trip me up. With different vowels it reads "my deceivers". Verse 7 says who they are: the rich who trust in wealth.

decisions.choice: Why should I fear?: the riddle
decisions.reason: This is the question the psalm answers: there is no need to fear the powerful rich.

decisions.choice: cheaters
decisions.reason: Readable follows the likeliest sense (m1).

source.text: הַבֹּטְחִ֥ים עַל־חֵילָ֑ם וּבְרֹ֥ב עָ֝שְׁרָ֗ם יִתְהַלָּֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: those who trust in their wealth, and in [the] abundance of their riches they boast?

en.L: those who trust in their wealth, and boast in the abundance of their riches?
en.B: people who rely on their money and brag about how rich they are?
en.R: They trust in their money and brag about how much they have.

fr.L: ceux qui se confient en leur fortune, et se vantent de l’abondance de leurs richesses ?
fr.B: ces gens qui comptent sur leur argent et se vantent de leurs grandes richesses ?
fr.R: Ils ont confiance en leur argent et se vantent d’en avoir beaucoup.

decisions.choice: those who trust: the rich of verse 6
decisions.reason: The verse explains who surrounds him: people whose confidence is in their wealth.

decisions.choice: trust in wealth: the wrong refuge
decisions.reason: Trusting in riches is set against trusting in God (52:9; Proverbs 11:28).

source.text: אָ֗ח לֹא־פָדֹ֣ה יִפְדֶּ֣ה אִ֑ישׁ לֹא־יִתֵּ֖ן לֵאלֹהִ֣ים כָּפְרֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: A brother, not he can at all ransom anyone; not he can give to God his ransom,

en.L: A brother — [one] cannot by any means ransom [him]; no one can give to God the ransom for [him],
en.B: No one can ever buy back the life of another, or pay God the price for that person's life,
en.R: No one can pay God enough to save someone else's life.

fr.L: Un frère — [on] ne peut en aucune façon [le] racheter ; nul ne peut donner à Dieu sa rançon,
fr.B: Personne ne pourra jamais racheter la vie d’un autre, ni payer à Dieu le prix de sa vie,
fr.R: Personne ne peut payer assez à Dieu pour sauver la vie de quelqu’un d’autre.

decisions.choice: a brother: no one can ransom even a brother
alternatives: surely (with different vowels): truly no one can ransom himself
decisions.reason: The Hebrew begins with "a brother": no one can buy back even a brother's life. With different vowels the word would mean "surely", and some Hebrew manuscripts read it so. Either way, no wealth can buy anyone free from death.

decisions.choice: ransom: a price paid to set a life free
decisions.reason: In the law, a ransom (kofer) could be paid for a life that was forfeit (Exodus 30:12). Before death no price is enough; only God can ransom (verse 16).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 9 is an aside and verse 10 finishes the thought ("that he should live on forever"), so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: וְ֭יֵקַר פִּדְי֥וֹן נַפְשָׁ֗ם וְחָדַ֥ל לְעוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and costly [is the] ransom of their soul, and it fails forever,

en.L: for the ransom of their soul is costly, and [it] fails forever,
en.B: for the price of a life is far too high, and no payment could ever be enough,
en.R: The price of a life is far too high. No one could ever pay it.

fr.L: car le rachat de leur âme est coûteux, et [il] manque pour toujours,
fr.B: car le prix d’une vie est bien trop élevé, et aucun paiement ne suffirait jamais,
fr.R: Le prix d’une vie est bien trop élevé. Personne ne pourrait jamais le payer.

decisions.choice: it fails forever: the payment can never be made
decisions.reason: The verb (chadal) means to stop or leave off: the ransom always falls short, or one must give up trying to pay it.

decisions.choice: their soul: their life
decisions.reason: Soul (nefesh) is the person's life itself, which is what is at stake.

decisions.choice: "âme" for nefesh at Literal, "vie" at Balanced and Readable, for this block of psalms
decisions.reason: Nefesh is the whole living person and its life (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the traditional word "âme", so the reader sees where nefesh stands; Balanced and Readable say "vie", "moi" or a plain pronoun, as the English does with "life" and "self".

source.text: וִֽיחִי־ע֥וֹד לָנֶ֑צַח לֹ֖א יִרְאֶ֣ה הַשָּֽׁחַת׃

records.literal_gloss: that he should live still forever, not see the pit.

en.L: that {{gender:they|he}} should live on forever [and] not see the pit.
en.B: so that anyone could live on forever and never see the grave.
en.R: Nobody can pay to live forever and never go down to the grave.

fr.L: pour qu’on vive encore à jamais [et] ne voie pas la fosse.
fr.B: pour que quelqu’un puisse vivre toujours sans jamais voir la tombe.
fr.R: Personne ne peut payer pour vivre toujours sans jamais descendre dans la tombe.

decisions.choice: the pit: the grave
decisions.reason: The pit (shachat) is the grave, the place of the dead (16:10; 30:10).

decisions.choice: see the pit: die
decisions.reason: To see a thing is to experience it; to see the pit is to die.

decisions.choice: they, with "he" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The verb is about anyone at all.

decisions.choice: no gender setting for "on" at Literal
decisions.reason: The English needs the setting on "they" or "he"; French "on" already means anyone, so the sentence needs none.

source.text: כִּ֤י יִרְאֶ֨ה׀חֲכָ֘מִ֤ים יָמ֗וּתוּ יַ֤חַד כְּסִ֣יל וָבַ֣עַר יֹאבֵ֑דוּ וְעָזְב֖וּ לַאֲחֵרִ֣ים חֵילָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For he sees [that] wise [people] die; together [the] fool and [the] stupid perish and leave to others their wealth.

en.L: For [one] sees [that the] wise die; together [the] fool and [the] dull perish and leave their wealth to others.
en.B: Anyone can see it: wise people die, and fools and dullards perish with them, handing over their wealth to others.
en.R: Everyone can see that even wise people die. Foolish and stupid people die too. Then other people get their money.

fr.L: Car [on] voit [que les] sages meurent ; ensemble [l’]insensé et [le] stupide périssent et laissent à d’autres leur fortune.
fr.B: Chacun le voit : les sages meurent, et l’insensé comme l’imbécile périssent avec eux, laissant leur fortune à d’autres.
fr.R: Tout le monde peut voir que même les sages meurent. Les insensés et les gens stupides meurent aussi. Puis d’autres prennent leur argent.

decisions.choice: he sees: anyone can see
decisions.reason: The subject of "sees" is not named; it is anyone who looks, or the rich man himself, who sees death all around and still trusts in his wealth.

decisions.choice: fool, stupid: people without sense
decisions.reason: The fool (kesil) and the brutish (ba'ar) are people who do not use the sense God gave them; the second word is related to the word for cattle (73:22).

decisions.choice: leave their wealth to others
decisions.reason: Ecclesiastes 2:18-21 makes the same complaint, and Jesus tells of a rich fool whose wealth goes to others (Luke 12:20).

source.text: קִרְבָּ֤ם בָּתֵּ֨ימוֹ׀לְֽעוֹלָ֗ם מִ֭שְׁכְּנֹתָם לְדֹ֣ר וָדֹ֑ר קָֽרְא֥וּ בִ֝שְׁמוֹתָ֗ם עֲלֵ֣י אֲדָמֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Their inward [thought: their] houses forever, their dwellings to generation and generation; they called by their names on lands.

en.L: Their inward [thought is that] their houses [are] forever, their dwelling places to generation and generation; they have called [their] lands by their own names.
en.B: They imagine their houses will last forever, their homes for all generations; they have named whole estates after themselves.
en.R: They think their houses will last forever and their families will live in them for all time. They name their lands after themselves.

fr.L: Leur pensée intime : leurs maisons [sont] pour toujours, leurs demeures de génération en génération ; ils ont appelé [leurs] terres de leurs noms.
fr.B: Ils s’imaginent que leurs maisons dureront toujours, leurs demeures pour toutes les générations ; ils ont donné leur nom à des domaines entiers.
fr.R: Ils pensent que leurs maisons dureront toujours et que leurs familles y vivront pour toujours. Ils donnent leur propre nom à leurs terres.

decisions.choice: their inward thought: what they think
alternatives: their graves (the ancient Greek translation): their graves are their homes forever
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "their inside", that is, their inner thought. The ancient Greek and Syriac translations read the same letters in a different order, "their graves": "their graves are their houses forever", a bitter irony. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: they called by their names on lands: they named estates after themselves
decisions.reason: To call land by one's name is to claim it as one's own (2 Samuel 12:28).

decisions.choice: They imagine (B); They think (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "their inward" means (m1).

source.text: וְאָדָ֣ם בִּ֭יקָר בַּל־יָלִ֑ין נִמְשַׁ֖ל כַּבְּהֵמ֣וֹת נִדְמֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: But humankind in honor not remains; he is like the animals [that] perish.

en.L: But {{gender:humankind|man}} in honor does not remain; {{gender:they are|he is}} like the animals [that] perish.
en.B: Yet no one, however honored, stays for long; humans are no different from animals that die.
en.R: Rich and famous people do not last forever. They die, just like animals.

fr.L: Mais {{gender:l’humain|l’homme}} dans l’honneur ne demeure pas ; il est semblable aux bêtes [qui] périssent.
fr.B: Pourtant personne, si honoré soit-il, ne reste longtemps ; {{gender:les humains|les hommes}} ne valent pas mieux que les bêtes qui meurent.
fr.R: Les gens riches et célèbres ne durent pas toujours. Ils meurent, comme les animaux.

decisions.choice: remain: stay, as for a night
alternatives: understand (some ancient translations, as in verse 21)
decisions.reason: The verb (lun) means to stay the night: honor is a lodging for one night only. Verse 21 repeats the line with one letter changed, "does not understand".

decisions.choice: honor: wealth and standing
decisions.reason: The word (yeqar) is preciousness: costly things, and the honor they bring.

decisions.choice: the refrain: the proverb of verse 5
decisions.reason: This line and verse 21 are the refrain of the psalm, probably the "proverb" announced in verse 5.

decisions.choice: humankind, they are (with "man", "he is" as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: The word ('adam) is human beings in general.

decisions.choice: "l'humain" (Literal) and "les humains" (Balanced), with "l'homme" and "les hommes" as the alternatives; the pronoun "il" that refers back takes no setting
decisions.reason: Adam here is human beings in general. French puts the setting on the noun only; the English also puts it on the pronoun, which French does not need, since "il" after "l'humain" is ordinary generic French.

source.text: זֶ֣ה דַ֭רְכָּם כֵּ֣סֶל לָ֑מוֹ וְאַחֲרֵיהֶ֓ם׀בְּפִיהֶ֖ם יִרְצ֣וּ סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: This [is] their way, folly [belongs] to them, and after them in their mouth they delight. Selah.

en.L: This [is] the way of those who have folly, and after them [people] delight in their mouth. Selah
en.B: Such is the road of the foolishly self-assured, and of those who come after them and like what they say. Selah
en.R: This is what happens to people who are sure of themselves. It also happens to those who follow them and agree with what they say. Selah

fr.L: Tel [est] le chemin de ceux qui ont de la folie, et après eux [on] se plaît à leur bouche. Sélah
fr.B: Tel est le chemin de ceux qui ont une sotte assurance, et de ceux qui viennent après eux et aiment ce qu’ils disent. Sélah
fr.R: Voilà ce qui arrive aux gens qui sont sûrs d’eux. Cela arrive aussi à ceux qui les suivent et approuvent ce qu’ils disent. Sélah

decisions.choice: folly: foolish confidence
decisions.reason: The word (kesel) can mean folly or confidence; here both: a confidence that is foolish.

decisions.choice: after them they delight in their mouth: followers approve their words
alternatives: after them they run to their own mouth
decisions.reason: The line is hard. It seems to say that people who come after them still admire what they said, though it led to death.

decisions.choice: their way: the road they take and where it ends
decisions.reason: Way (derek) is a path of life and its end, as in 1:6.

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: כַּצֹּ֤אן׀לִֽשְׁא֣וֹל שַׁתּוּ֮ מָ֤וֶת יִ֫רְעֵ֥ם וַיִּרְדּ֘וּ בָ֤ם יְשָׁרִ֨ים׀לַבֹּ֗קֶר וְ֭צוּרָם לְבַלּ֥וֹת שְׁא֗וֹל מִזְּבֻ֥ל לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Like the sheep for Sheol they are appointed; death will shepherd them, and [the] upright will rule over them in the morning; and their form [is] for Sheol to wear away, from [a] lofty dwelling for it.

en.L: Like sheep they are appointed for Sheol; death will shepherd them, and [the] upright will rule over them in the morning; and their form [is] for Sheol to wear away, [with] no lofty dwelling for it.
en.B: Like sheep they are herded into Sheol, and Death is their shepherd. The upright will rule over them when morning comes; their bodies will waste away in Sheol, far from their grand houses.
en.R: Like sheep, they are headed for the place of the dead. Death will lead them like a shepherd. In the morning, good people will rule over them. Their bodies will rot in the grave, far away from their fine homes.

fr.L: Comme des brebis ils sont destinés au Shéol ; la mort les fera paître, et [les hommes] droits domineront sur eux au matin ; et leur forme [est] pour le Shéol, qui l’usera, sans haute demeure pour elle.
fr.B: Comme des brebis on les mène au séjour des morts, et la Mort est leur berger. Les hommes droits domineront sur eux quand viendra le matin ; leur corps s’usera au séjour des morts, loin de leurs riches maisons.
fr.R: Comme des moutons, ils vont vers le séjour des morts. La mort les conduira comme un berger. Au matin, les gens droits régneront sur eux. Leur corps pourrira dans la tombe, loin de leurs belles maisons.

decisions.choice: death will shepherd them: they are led to death like sheep
decisions.reason: Death is pictured as a shepherd driving its flock into Sheol, the place of the dead. The proud rich are like animals (verse 13), and end like them.

decisions.choice: the upright will rule over them in the morning
decisions.reason: Morning is the time of God's help after a night of danger (46:6). When God acts, the upright, who feared the rich, will be over them.

decisions.choice: their form ... no lofty dwelling: a hard line
decisions.reason: The end of the verse is very hard. The word for "their form" is read in place of a written form meaning "their rock", and the last words read literally "from a lofty dwelling for it", that is, without a home, or far from their fine houses. The general sense is that their bodies waste away in Sheol.

decisions.choice: Sheol: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place where the dead go, pictured as below the earth (6:6).

decisions.choice: the place of the dead
decisions.reason: Readable says what Sheol is.

decisions.choice: "le Shéol" (Literal); "le séjour des morts" (Balanced, Readable), for this block of psalms
alternatives: "le Shéol" at Balanced, as the English Balanced keeps "Sheol"
decisions.reason: Sheol is the place of the dead (meaning decision m4). Literal keeps the name; Balanced and Readable use the usual French phrase for it, as this translation does throughout. "L'enfer" would add the idea of punishment.

source.text: אַךְ־אֱלֹהִ֗ים יִפְדֶּ֣ה נַ֭פְשִׁי מִֽיַּד־שְׁא֑וֹל כִּ֖י יִקָּחֵ֣נִי סֶֽלָה׃

records.literal_gloss: Surely God will ransom my soul from [the] hand of Sheol, for he will take me. Selah.

en.L: But God will ransom my soul from the hand of Sheol, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will take me. Selah
en.B: But God will pay the ransom for my life and free it from Sheol's grip, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will take me. Selah
en.R: But God will pay the price to save my life from the place of the dead. He will take me to be with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Selah

fr.L: Mais Dieu rachètera mon âme de la main du Shéol, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me prendra. Sélah
fr.B: Mais Dieu paiera la rançon de ma vie et l’arrachera à l’emprise du séjour des morts, car {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} me prendra. Sélah
fr.R: Mais Dieu paiera le prix pour sauver ma vie du séjour des morts. Il me prendra pour que je sois avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Sélah

decisions.choice: God will ransom my soul: what no one else can do
decisions.reason: No human can pay the ransom for a life (verses 8-9), but God can, and will. This is the answer to the riddle of verse 6.

decisions.choice: he will take me: as God took Enoch and Elijah
decisions.reason: The verb (laqach) is the one used when God took Enoch (Genesis 5:24) and Elijah (2 Kings 2:3, 5). The psalmist hopes that death will not have the last word over him (compare 73:24). How much he saw of life after death is not spelled out.

decisions.choice: the hand of Sheol: the power of death
decisions.reason: The hand is power; Sheol holds the dead in its grip.

decisions.choice: to be with him
decisions.reason: Readable says what "take me" means (m2).

decisions.choice: Selah: a word whose meaning is no longer known
alternatives: lift up (the voice or the music)
decisions.reason: Selah stands at the end of a line 71 times in the Psalms and 3 times in Habakkuk 3. It is probably a direction for singing or music, perhaps a pause or an interlude; the ancient Greek translation renders it with a word meaning "interlude". It is not part of what is said, and here it marks a break after the line.

decisions.choice: Selah, kept as it is
decisions.reason: Its meaning is unknown (see the meaning decision on Selah), so every level keeps the word rather than guess, and keeps it apart from the sentence.

source.text: אַל־תִּ֭ירָא כִּֽי־יַעֲשִׁ֣ר אִ֑ישׁ כִּֽי־יִ֝רְבֶּה כְּב֣וֹד בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Do not fear when [a] man becomes rich, when the honor of his house increases,

en.L: Do not fear when {{gender:someone|a man}} becomes rich, when the glory of {{gender:their|his}} house increases,
en.B: Do not be alarmed when someone gets rich and their household gains in wealth and honor,
en.R: Do not be upset when someone gets rich and their family becomes more and more important.

fr.L: Ne crains pas quand quelqu’un s’enrichit, quand la gloire de sa maison s’accroît,
fr.B: Ne t’inquiète pas quand quelqu’un devient riche et que sa maison gagne en richesse et en honneur,
fr.R: Ne sois pas troublé quand quelqu’un devient riche et que sa famille devient de plus en plus importante.

decisions.choice: Do not fear: the lesson
decisions.reason: The teacher now speaks to the hearer, answering the question of verse 6.

decisions.choice: the honor of his house: his household's wealth and standing
decisions.reason: Honor (kavod) is weight: wealth, and the importance it brings (Genesis 31:1).

decisions.choice: someone, their (with "a man", "his" as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: The word ('ish) means anyone who grows rich.

decisions.choice: "quelqu'un" with no gender setting, here and in verses 18-20
decisions.reason: The English puts the setting on "someone" and on the pronouns that follow. French "quelqu'un" already means anyone, and the "il", "sa" and "lui" that refer back to it are ordinary generic French, so these verses need no setting.

source.text: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א בְ֭מוֹתוֹ יִקַּ֣ח הַכֹּ֑ל לֹא־יֵרֵ֖ד אַחֲרָ֣יו כְּבוֹדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: for not in his death will he take anything; not will go down after him his honor.

en.L: for when {{gender:they die they|he dies he}} will take nothing; {{gender:their|his}} glory will not go down after {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: for when they die they can take none of it with them; their splendor will not follow them down.
en.R: When they die, they cannot take anything with them. Their riches and honor will not go down into the grave with them.

fr.L: car dans sa mort il n’emportera rien ; sa gloire ne descendra pas après lui.
fr.B: car à sa mort il ne pourra rien emporter ; sa splendeur ne le suivra pas en bas.
fr.R: Quand il mourra, il ne pourra rien emporter. Sa richesse et son honneur ne descendront pas avec lui dans la tombe.

decisions.choice: he will take nothing: naked into the grave
decisions.reason: Compare Job 1:21, Ecclesiastes 5, and 1 Timothy 6:7.

decisions.choice: go down: to Sheol
decisions.reason: The dead "go down" to Sheol (55:16); their glory stays behind.

decisions.choice: they, their, them (with "he", "his", "him" as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

source.text: כִּֽי־נַ֭פְשׁוֹ בְּחַיָּ֣יו יְבָרֵ֑ךְ וְ֝יוֹדֻ֗ךָ כִּי־תֵיטִ֥יב לָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Though his soul in his life he blesses — and they praise you when you do well for yourself —

en.L: Though in {{gender:their|his}} life {{gender:they bless their|he blesses his}} soul — and [people] praise you when you do well for yourself —
en.B: Though in life they count themselves blessed — and people praise you when you prosper —
en.R: While they are alive, they may think they are very happy. People may speak highly of you when you are doing well.

fr.L: Bien que durant sa vie il bénisse son âme — et [on] te loue quand tu te fais du bien —
fr.B: Bien que de son vivant il se félicite lui-même — et l’on te loue quand tu prospères —
fr.R: Pendant sa vie, il pense peut-être qu’il est très heureux. On dit peut-être du bien de toi quand tout te réussit.

decisions.choice: he blesses his soul: he congratulates himself
decisions.reason: To bless one's own soul is to tell oneself how well one is doing (compare Luke 12:19).

decisions.choice: you: the teacher speaks to the rich man
decisions.reason: In the middle of the sentence the teacher turns to address the rich man himself, or anyone tempted to be like him: people praise you when you prosper. "You" is not God.

decisions.choice: their, they bless (with "his", "he blesses" as the alternatives)
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

source.text: תָּ֭בוֹא עַד־דּ֣וֹר אֲבוֹתָ֑יו עַד־נֵ֝֗צַח לֹ֣א יִרְאוּ־אֽוֹר׃

records.literal_gloss: it will go to [the] generation of his fathers; until forever not they will see light.

en.L: it will go to the generation of {{gender:their|his}} fathers; they will never see light.
en.B: they will go to join the generation of their ancestors, who will never again see the light.
en.R: But they will die and join their ancestors in the dark, where no one ever sees light again.

fr.L: il ira jusqu’à la génération de ses pères ; ils ne verront jamais la lumière.
fr.B: il ira rejoindre la génération de ses ancêtres, qui ne reverront jamais la lumière.
fr.R: Mais il mourra et rejoindra ses ancêtres dans le noir, où personne ne voit plus jamais la lumière.

decisions.choice: it will go: his soul will go
decisions.reason: The verb can be read "it will go", with "his soul" of verse 19 as its subject, or "you will go", continuing the address to the rich man.

decisions.choice: go to the generation of his fathers: die
decisions.reason: To join one's ancestors is to die (Genesis 15:15).

decisions.choice: see light: be alive
decisions.reason: Light is life (56:14; Job 33:30). The dead in Sheol do not see it.

decisions.choice: their, with "his" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

source.text: אָדָ֣ם בִּ֭יקָר וְלֹ֣א יָבִ֑ין נִמְשַׁ֖ל כַּבְּהֵמ֣וֹת נִדְמֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Humankind in honor and not he understands is like the animals [that] perish.

en.L: {{gender:Humankind|Man}} in honor, and not understanding, is like the animals [that] perish.
en.B: A person held in honor who does not understand is no different from animals that die.
en.R: Rich and famous people who do not understand this will die like animals.

fr.L: {{gender:L’humain|L’homme}} dans l’honneur, et qui ne comprend pas, est semblable aux bêtes [qui] périssent.
fr.B: {{gender:Un être humain|Un homme}} comblé d’honneur, s’il ne comprend pas, ne vaut pas mieux que les bêtes qui meurent.
fr.R: Les gens riches et célèbres qui ne comprennent pas cela mourront comme les animaux.

decisions.choice: does not understand: the refrain with a twist
decisions.reason: The refrain of verse 13 returns with one letter changed: not "does not remain" but "does not understand". It is not honor that makes people like the animals, but honor without understanding, the understanding the psalm has taught.

decisions.choice: honor
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.

decisions.choice: Humankind, with "Man" as the alternative
decisions.reason: As in verse 13.
